issue_context.title: Go2rtc raises 400 on Unifi Protect camera
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Since the https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/130139 workaround for go2rtc in 2024.11.1 it has caused mine to stop functioning with Unifi Protect and fallback to HLS.

I couldn't find a way to download diagnostic data but did testing via the debug_ui.

I was thinking is that it could be HA trying to spin up an RTSP redirect while Unifi Protect is using RTSPS.  I can load the redirect streams directly, both the original and non original version it spins up, via the embedded go2rtc and those work fine.  So I believe the embedded go2rtc is functioning but something breaks the connection between it and HA.  I only have Unifi Protect cameras and no other way to see if other cameras are impacted.


This may get resolved with the upstream patch to go2rtc if it negates the need to spin up redirect streams to avoid that bug.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2024.11.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2024.11.0

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

go2rtc

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/go2rtc/

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Do you see any logs in go2rtc?

The above log is raised when adding the original stream, so I'm not sure how you did test the following:

> I can load the redirect streams directly, both the original and non original version it spins up, via the embedded go2rtc and those work fine.

As both streams were not added to go2rtc. Did you manually add them to go2rtc?

I enabled the **debug_ui** and from there everything appears to work properly, no errors in the logs because it was working.  I didn't manually add anything in there. When I would try to load a stream in HA, or load a page with streams, it would auto-create / populate them.

From the above error, the workaround is not the issue, as it's probably the stream source is not accepted by go2rtc.
Nevertheless, the workaround will be removed as they were fixed upstream.

review_comments: Should we also change the minimum version in the go2rtc client's version check?

If we update the min. version it would be a breaking change and not allowed in the patch release.
Also, the code still works with go2rtc. Only changing the log level will not work.

> If we update the min. version it would be a breaking change and not allowed in the patch release.

I'm not sure I agree requiring users who decide to manage the go2rtc server by themselves to upgrade to a good version of go2rtc can be considered a breaking change.
